course_summary:
ISEN 627 | Engineering Analysis for Decision Making | Fall 2026
Instructor: Alexander Abuabara | abuabara@tamu.edu
Meets: MWF 11:30AM - 12:20PM | ETB 1027
Grading: Exams [60%], Project [30%], Participation [10%] — A: ≥ 90%; B: ≥ 80%; C: ≥ 70%; D: ≥ 60%; F: <60%
Topics: MCMC, Approximate Bayesian Computation, Conjugate Priors, Poisson Processes, Mark and Recapture, Survival Analysis, Bayes's Theorem, Bayesian approaches to perception, computational models for Bayesian inference, strategic decision support, utility theory, information theory, quantification of information for decision-making, Estimating Proportions, Estimating Counts, Odds and Addends, Minimum, Maximum, Mixture, Decision Analysis, Testing, Comparison, Classification, Inference, Linear Regression, Logistic Regression, Probability, Distributions, techniques in analysis of decision processes, engineering systems under uncertainty, concepts from economics, psychology, management science, analyze decision-making processes
Tools: Canvas
Prerequisites: ISEN 609; STAT 601 or approval of instructor

headers.text: E-mail is the primary method of communication. Include the course number in the subject line. Responses should not be expected after 5:00 PM, on weekends, or on holidays.
